**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on behaving inappropriately in eight ways

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pārājika 8, titled *Aṭṭhavatthukā* ("The training rule on behaving inappropriately in eight ways"), is the eighth and final rule entailing expulsion (*pārājika*) for fully ordained nuns in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a nun who consents to all eight forms of flirtatious misconduct with an impassioned man commits an offense of defeat and is expelled from the community. Biblically and structurally, this is the first among a substantial group of rules in the Vinaya whose origin story features the notorious group of six nuns (*chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo*), who were either affiliated with or literary counterparts to the group of six monks. A complete modern English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 In other Vinaya lineages, the rule corresponds to the sixth *pārājika*, designated either as *Aṭṭhavatthukā* in the Mahāsāṃghika and Lokottaravāda traditions, or under the title *Vajjappaṭicchādikā* in the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda recensions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan.
